## Production workflow

- Plan the hook (ChatGPT, Claude): I find the angle, write hook options and the script, then break the ad into scenes with a detailed prompt for each one.
- Generate the scenes (Google Flow, Vibe): Google Flow generates the video scenes, and Vibe brings still images to life. I refine every shot until the characters and the product stay consistent.
- Give it a voice (AI Studio, Gemini): AI Studio voices the script in a tone matched to your customer, and Gemini creates the music underneath.
- Add motion graphics (Claude): Claude helps me build animated overlays, like news tickers, route maps, rate cards and kinetic text, so the details land on screen.
- Automate the build (Claude Code): Claude Code writes and runs my build scripts: it cuts every hook variation from one edit list, checks AI clips frame by frame for glitches and wrong logos, lays in captions and graphics, and mixes the audio to -14 LUFS.
- Edit and finish (CapCut): Everything comes together in CapCut: pacing, cuts, captions, sound effects and the final mix.
- Brand visuals (Canva, Canva AI): Posters and social graphics that match the ad, designed in Canva with help from Canva AI.

## Projects

### 1. Stepprs: 3, 2, 1 Reveal (4 Hook Variations)

- Brand: Stepprs
- Creative style: 8-Figure E-commerce
- Concept: A dropship-style countdown reveal. The orange glowing through a thin white towel teases the product before the pull.
- Description: Four 11-second shareable reveal ads for Stepprs massage insoles. A towel or hi-vis vest hides the shoes, a voice counts down 3, 2, 1, and the bright orange insoles are pulled out from under it, then pressed and walked on. Each version speaks to a different customer.
- Hook: One relatable complaint on screen (“My feet are killing me after work”), then “Me:” and a spoken 3, 2, 1 countdown.
- Audience: Shift workers in steel-toe boots, people with everyday foot pain, people with morning heel pain, and daily walkers
- Objective: Get the ad shared: every version ends on a “send this to…” caption aimed at the viewer's friends or coworkers.
- AI generation and production tools: Google Flow, Nano Banana, Gemini (voice), Claude Code, FFmpeg
- Production: AI scenes from approved keyframes in Google Flow, with the real Stepprs heel logo and node layout checked frame by frame and corrected where the AI got it wrong. Orange step-glow rings on the walk-out.
- Editing: Cuts timed to the reference's beat, a caption swap from the complaint to the share line, countdown voiceover over the music bed, mixed to -14 LUFS.
- Claude Code editing and automation workflow: Claude Code writes and runs my build scripts: it cuts every hook variation from one edit list, checks AI clips frame by frame for glitches and wrong logos, lays in captions and graphics, and mixes the audio to -14 LUFS.
- Deliverables: 4 vertical (9:16) ads, about 11 seconds each, for TikTok, Reels, Meta and Snapchat.
- Format: 9:16, 0:11
- Video URL: https://angelyn-portfolio.vercel.app/stepprs-321-steeltoe.mp4
- Variant video — Steel toe (hook: My feet are killing me after work. Me: 3, 2, 1…): https://angelyn-portfolio.vercel.app/stepprs-321-steeltoe.mp4
- Variant video — Everyday pain (hook: My feet hurt every single day. Me: 3, 2, 1…): https://angelyn-portfolio.vercel.app/stepprs-321-girlfriend.mp4
- Variant video — Heel pain (hook: I hate waking up with heel pain. Me: 3, 2, 1…): https://angelyn-portfolio.vercel.app/stepprs-321-heelpain.mp4
- Variant video — Walker (hook: How do you walk 10k steps every day? Me: 3, 2, 1…): https://angelyn-portfolio.vercel.app/stepprs-321-walker.mp4

- Audience: Adults 35+ with first-step-in-the-morning heel pain

- AI generation and production tools: Google Flow, Nano Banana, Claude Code, FFmpeg
- Production: AI before/after scenes in Google Flow with real brand footage for the insole insert, so the product is always accurate. Characters, props and set checked for continuity across shots.

- Claude Code editing and automation workflow: Claude Code writes and runs my build scripts: it cuts every hook variation from one edit list, checks AI clips frame by frame for glitches and wrong logos, lays in captions and graphics, and mixes the audio to -14 LUFS.

- Hook: A macro cork release, then bubbles and her lips on the wine at the rim: “An unexpected origin.”
- Audience: Wine lovers who would not expect great sparkling wine from the Douro
- Objective: Introduce a Douro sparkling wine with a premium, sensory feel and keep the real bottle exactly as it looks on the shelf.
- AI generation and production tools: Google Flow, Nano Banana, Claude Code, FFmpeg
- Production: Four AI scenes generated in Google Flow from approved keyframes and character references (bubbles, the sip, the pour, the raised glass). Every product shot is real client footage or the client's own bottle photo, with no generated bottle, label or foil.
- Editing: Captions in Poppins (the brief's typeface) kept inside the Reels safe area, one grade and grain across real and AI shots, a synced cork pop, pour and fizz, licensed music mixed to -17 LUFS, and a dark end card with the Wine Portugal logo. A textless version was also delivered for the German edit.
- Claude Code editing and automation workflow: Claude Code writes and runs my build scripts: it cuts every hook variation from one edit list, checks AI clips frame by frame for glitches and wrong logos, lays in captions and graphics, and mixes the audio to -14 LUFS.
- Deliverables: 20-second vertical (9:16) English ad, plus a textless version for localization.

### 9. Sunster Self-Tanner: Grey to Golden (Danish)

- Brand: Sunster
- Creative style: Product & DTC Ads
- Concept: A time-stamped night-to-morning story (22:00 to 07:00 to Day 5) that makes the result feel real and the routine feel easy.
- Description: A Danish-language DTC ad for Sunster self-tanner that follows one night from winter-pale to golden: the 22:00 routine, the glow developing overnight, the 07:00 reveal, and a friend asking if she's been on vacation.
- Hook: “Vinterbleg?” (Winter pale?) “Ingen sol før april… og jeg ligner et spøgelse.” (No sun until April… and I look like a ghost.)
- Audience: Danish women who feel pale during the long, sunless winter
- Objective: Show the full routine and believable results, then drive purchases of the self-tanning set.
- AI generation and production tools: Not listed
- Production: Live-action AI scenes with on-screen clock timestamps, a step-by-step routine (drops in day cream for the face, mousse and mitt for the body, 10 minutes), a skin close-up showing the glow developing over 6–8 hours, and a before-and-after mirror shot.
- Editing: Danish captions with highlighted keywords, step cards and a progress bar, a before/after split, and social proof on Day 5 (“Har du været på ferie?” – Have you been on vacation?). End card: “Danmarks bedste selvbruner”, Danish Beauty Award 2025 nominee, “Køb sættet nu” (Buy the set now), 45-day risk-free trial.
- Deliverables: 30-second vertical (9:16) ad in Danish for TikTok, Reels and Shorts.
- Format: 9:16, 0:30
- Video URL: https://angelyn-portfolio.vercel.app/sunster-grey-to-golden.mp4

CTA: “Prøv risikofrit i 45 dage” (Try it risk-free for 45 days), sunster.dk.
